title: Customer preflight manifest + Edge Bridge fastlane for constrained-network private deployments
creator: Aria Patel
description:
Goal: Provide a deterministic, low-friction intake + prioritization path for enterprise customers who request Private/VPC/on-prem deployments but are blocked by constrained networking (air-gapped sites, restricted egress, and legacy proxy topologies).

Problem statement:
- Sales and Customer Success frequently surface requests that are technically feasible but require bespoke networking changes or temporary exceptions that the customer cannot approve without a clear security and rollout plan.
- Current intake is ad hoc: engineering spends significant time triaging one-off asks; legal/security reviews are reactive; onboarding slips because we lack an automated preflight manifest and a narrow "fastlane" pattern customers can accept.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) "Preflight Manifest" generator: a JSON/YAML manifest customers can run internally (or provide to their network team) that enumerates minimal required connectivity, IPs, ports, TLS expectations, and an explicit risk statement per connector. The manifest also contains a reversible staging plan (timeboxed egress tunnel, limited CIDR, allowed domains).
2) Edge Bridge fastlane pattern: an opinionated connector template and runbook for customers who can temporarily allow a narrow outbound bridge (eg, a short-lived proxy tunnel) to enable initial onboarding and telemetry while preserving long-term airgap posture.
3) Prioritization rubric: a transparent scoring model to decide which requests get the fastlane vs bespoke engineering effort. Scores will consider: regulatory constraints, size of ARR uplift, operational complexity, reusability of the solution, and security risk.
4) Triage workflow: intake form + automated scoring -> PM review -> Security gate (auto-flag high-risk) -> Engineering spike or fastlane enablement -> Success-led onboarding.

Intake form fields (customer-visible):
- Customer name, account ID, region
- Deployment mode requested (VPC / on-prem / hybrid)
- Network constraints (full airgap / limited egress windows / proxy-only outbound)
- Critical endpoints the product must reach (S3, model registry, control plane, metrics endpoint)
- Data classification and compliance regime (e.g., HIPAA, PCI, GDPR)
- Desired timeline and business justification
- Willingness to accept temporary narrow egress/bridge (yes/no)

Prioritization rubric (weights example):
- Business impact (ARR uplift / customer urgency): 30
- Regulatory difficulty (compliance + audit burden): 25
- Reusability (will solution generalize to other customers?): 20
- Engineering effort (estimated points): 15 (inverse scoring)
- Security risk (residual exposure after mitigations): 10 (auto-flag if > threshold)
Total score -> routing: Fastlane enablement (>=70) | Engineering design + tactical sprint (50-69) | Defer/custom roadmap (>50 but high risk)

Acceptance criteria:
- Preflight manifest templates for 3 common enterprise profiles produced (fully airgapped, limited egress window, corporate-proxy-only) and validated with 2 pilot customers.
- Edge Bridge fastlane implementation docs + Terraform/Helm connector templates created and reviewed by Security and Infra teams.
- Intake form implemented in the Console requests page with automated scoring and email notifications to PM/SE.
- Rollout plan with playbooks for one pilot (Customer X) and measurable onboarding SLA (time-to-first-successful-API-call < 14 days for fastlane).

Out-of-scope for initial phase:
- Complete on-prem install automation or long-term airgap certifications (those are separate follow-ups).
- Building custom firmware/proxies for customer networks.

Operational safeguards and mitigations:
- Fastlane connector is timeboxed by default (7-day TTL) and limited to a narrow CIDR and set of hostnames; automatic expiry and telemetry for disconnection are enforced.
- Audit logs are required on both Redwood and customer side; we will collect a minimal telemetry set and disable any data-plane transfers aside from control-plane heartbeats unless customer opts in.
- Security and Legal sign-off required before enabling fastlane for any customer with regulated data.

Metrics / success criteria:
- Reduction in average triage time from intake to plan (baseline: ~18 days -> target: <7 days)
- % of private deployment customers who accept fastlane vs bespoke solution (target 40% fastlane adoption in first 6 months)
- Number of engineering hours saved per triaged request (target: 6h/request in month 1)

Rollout plan:
- Week 0-2: Finalize manifest templates + intake form schema. Design review with DES-1299.
- Week 2-4: Security + Legal alignment, build prototype connector templates (ENG-2184 spike).
- Week 4-6: Pilot with 2 willing customers (CS-led). Iterate manifest and scoring weights.
- Week 7+: Expand to broader cohort, instrument metrics, start productizing templates in Console release private-2026.04.

Risks and open questions:
- Some customers will deem any outbound connectivity unacceptable; need explicit escalation play for full bespoke on-prem install.
- Legal/regulatory teams may require additional audit artifacts, increasing effort per request.
- We must ensure fastlane templates do not create a persistent support burden or security liability if misconfigured by customer teams.

Next steps (this ticket):
- Lock intake schema and sample manifests (PM) [3 days].
- Schedule design workshop with DES-1299 for manifest readability and customer network-team handoff docs [owner: Marcus].
- Kick off Eng spike ENG-2184 to prototype a minimal Edge Bridge (timeboxed) and document required runtime changes (owner: Eng infra lead).
- Legal/Security sync to define mandatory audit artifacts and final approval checklist (owner: PM).
